newsitem.title: UK: George Wimpey sees good UK profit margins.
newsitem.headline: George Wimpey sees good UK profit margins.

text.p: British homebuilder George Wimpey Plc said on Thursday that UK profit margins from Wimpey and McLean homes were "significantly" ahead of last year.
"(This) augurs well for a further substantial increase in profits for the year as a whole," chairman Joe Dwyer told the annual general meeting.
Wimpey and McLean Homes are both achieving completions ahead of last year. Wimpey gained the McLean housing business from Tarmac Plc as part of an asset swap in 1995.
Dywer said that while house prices had risen strongly in London, that particular market was "unique" and he expected a price correction within the next two years.

"The rest of the country has moved into what I would call the classic recovery phase, with modest price inflation radiating out from the south east to all part of the UK by the end of the year," he said.

Structural changes being undertaken by the group should be completed by the year-end when it will comprise 28 companies in the UK, eight in the United States and three in Australia, together with reduced corporate centre in Hammersmith, London.
Dwyer said its U.S. and Australian businesses were still expanding rapidly with a further 40 to 50 percent increase planned for the year.
"Both businesses should make profitable contributions to the group this year," Dwyer added.
